newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Blast rocks Israeli missile factory.
newsitem.headline: Blast rocks Israeli missile factory.

text.p: An explosion tore through a warehouse on Sunday at a factory where Israel makes parts for the U.S.-funded Arrow anti-missile missile, injuring at least one person, a company official said.

It did not appear from initial reports that any production facilities at the state-owned Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) plant in the town of Beer Yaakov, near Tel Aviv, were damaged in the blast, which Israel Radio said was accidental.
Black smoke billowed over the plant and police said one person was treated for smoke inhalation.
A police spokeswoman gave no cause for the explosion but Israel Radio said paint and fuel in the storage area were accidently ignited during welding work.

An IAI official, who asked not to be identified, and Israel Television said the plant makes parts for the Arrow missile. The missile, designed to intercept incoming ballistic missiles, was last test fired over the Mediterranean on March 11.

The Arrow is jointly financed by Israel and the United States. Security sources estimate the countries have poured $500 millon into the project since 1991. The projected cost is $1.6 billion but analysts say it could cost many times that figure.
Israel has been on high alert for suicide bombings by Moslem militants since an attack on March 21 in a Tel Aviv cafe killed three Israeli women.
